title: Stateful consultant runtime should be atom/workflow-native instead of Badgey-specific
wanted_capability: A reusable stateful consultant primitive that exposes instance identity, resumable session binding, proposal lifecycle, action journaling, and workflow-visible apply/dispatch through atom contracts and workflow nodes, so Badgey is one configured consumer rather than a bespoke daemon feature.
missing_primitive: Atom/workflow-native consultant runtime with generic instance registry, proposal store, action journal, intent post-processor, and split apply protocol.
fallback_used: Badgey implements these facilities through bespoke badgey_* MCP tools, BadgeyId, BadgeyRegistry, ProposalStore under state_dir/badgey, bg-action-* note parsing, and Badgey-specific workflow MCP calls.
notes:
Existing workflow machinery already supports atom_bindings, workflow-backed atoms, hook mcp_call, foreach/subworkflow fanout, gates, actor_failure=continue, and structured workflow handles. Badgey apply/triage workflows show the desired direction, but the core consultant state remains outside atom invocation ownership/effects/composition.

DISSOLUTION DESIGN: design/orchestration/agents/consultant-runtime.md (thread-a6523755, badgey-dissolution worktree). Badgey was a forcing function for system primitives but the extraction never happened — the generic machinery (ProposalStore, ActionJournal, ResumeQueue, instance registry, split-apply, intent post-processor, restart restore/recover) all shipped Badgey-named. Dissolution concerns, in full in the design doc §4: (1) persisted-state migration of state_dir/badgey/{proposals,action_journal} incl. mid-flight non-terminal entries, locks, _archive/; (2) notes are load-bearing state — registry is RESTORED from Exec ThreadEvent notes + "badgey:<id>" thread names, and observability counters derive from note scans; legacy grammar must parse forever; (3) bg-action-* intent grammar is split across persona lens (prompt) and post-processor (parser) — they must move together or intents silently drop; (4) the wrapper post-processor is the recursion-guard security boundary — consumer descriptors must select from code-owned allowlisted action handlers, never define new ones in data, and get install-time gating like dispatch adapters; (5) system-defaults/badgey/ workflows/packets/crons call badgey_* tools by name via mcp_call — shim layer must outlive re-pointing, tool_docs.rs must track shims; (6) Slack channel bindings persist badgey_id on disk (data compat, not just rename); (7) proposal idempotency keys ((kind,draft)) and journal first-write idempotency must survive bit-for-bit or upgrades double-apply; (8) workflow coupling at src/workflow/schema.rs:22 + engine/actor_nodes.rs:152 must be replaced with consumer-agnostic shapes, not a second special case; (9) ~28 unit tests + eval/badgey/ harness move with the code to prove behavior preservation; (10) atom-contract fit — instances are long-lived, invocations are turns; atom_status reports the turn, the instance outlives any invocation. Phasing: P1 mechanical extraction to src/orchestration/consultant/ (no behavior change), P2 consumer descriptor boundary, P3 atom/workflow-native surface + consultant_* tools with badgey_* shims, P4 state migration + retirement.
